task: Explain why the sky appears blue.
text: The sky appears blue because sunlight is scattered by molecules in the atmosphere. Shorter blue wavelengths scatter more than longer red ones, so blue light reaches our eyes from all directions.

text: A moving bicycle stays upright mainly because of how steering corrects balance. When it begins to lean, the front wheel turns slightly into the lean, moving the wheels back under the center of mass.

task: Explain what causes the seasons to change.
text: Earth spins on an axis that is tilted relative to its orbital plane. As the planet travels around the sun, each hemisphere leans toward the sun for part of the year and away for the rest.

task: Explain how a rainbow forms.
text: Sunlight entering a raindrop bends, reflects off the back surface, and bends again on the way out. Different colors bend by slightly different amounts, so the white light spreads into a band of hues.

task: Explain why ice floats on water.
text: Water molecules form an open hexagonal lattice when they freeze, held apart by hydrogen bonds. That arrangement takes up more room than liquid water, so ice is less dense and rides on the surface.
